serverInfo.name: agent-cost-analyzer
serverInfo.title: Agent Cost Analyzer
serverInfo.description: Token, AI Credits and tool-call analysis of your local AI coding-agent sessions, by Raul Kivi.

withoutViews.instructions:
Read-only analyzer of local AI coding-agent logs (GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code, Claude Code CLI, pi, mitmproxy captures). It never writes, executes or reaches the network.

Workflow: find a session with list_sessions (query/since/until), then drill in with get_session_cost (spend), get_session_audit and list_tool_calls (tool-call failures), and get_turn (one turn's prompt, response, usage and calls). For trends use get_cost_rollup, get_audit_rollup and list_findings (security, anomalies, behaviour changes).

Scope: per-session tools and get_audit_rollup read one provider, the `provider` argument or else the one active in the web app (list_log_providers shows activeProviderId). get_cost_rollup and list_findings read every available provider unless `provider` is given.

Units: token counts are tokens; AI Credits are GitHub Copilot's billing unit and only VS Code sessions record them. A null figure is unknown, never zero: check knownTurns vs turns and unavailableReasons before comparing. `estimated` marks local-tokenizer estimates.

Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD or a timestamp), inclusive, compared against each session's start.

Cost by repository and project: list_repositories and list_projects first, then get_project_cost or get_repository_cost (over time, by vendor and model) or compare_costs (several side by side), then explain_cost_change (usage, price and mix effects) and get_price_changes for the price changes behind it.

Cost bases: billed is what the vendor billed (GitHub Copilot's AI Credits); reported is a cost the log itself records; priced is tokens × the price book's price for that model, channel and date (get_price_book lists the versions and their sources). The preferred basis takes billed, then reported, then priced; every total says how many turns it covers.

Prices: "as of use" (the default) prices each turn at the prices in force when it ran; "today's prices" reprices every turn at today's, to compare usage without price changes.

Conversion: 1 AI Credit = $0.01 (GitHub's documented rate); no other exchange rate is used.

Replay on another model: replay_session (one model, per turn) and compare_models_for_session (several, totals) run a session's own request trace through another model's caching rules and prices. Their figures are Simulated, assuming the same conversation and token counts: say "would have cost about". Check selfCheck (the replay on the session's own model against its log) and coverage (turns not replayed, with reasons) before relying on them.

Billing: get_statement reads a project's statement for a period; statements are issued only in the app, never by a tool. estimate_cost gives the cost of planned work as a p50–p90 range at today's prices, never one number; with `model`, on that model, simulated by replaying the project's sessions.

tools.name: compare_costs
tools.title: Compare repositories or projects
tools.description: Compares 2 to 20 repositories (keys from list_repositories) or projects (ids from list_projects) over one period: per id the total with coverage, the change against the previous period (or the same dates last year), cost per session, per active day and per turn, share of the compared total, cache-hit ratio and output share. Money measures are per currency unless currency is "usd"; a change against a period with nothing known is null, never "from 0". Defaults: the preferred basis, prices as of use, native currencies, the previous period. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: compare_models_for_session
tools.title: Compare models for a session
tools.description: Use to compare what one session (id from list_sessions) would have cost on several models: each model's simulated total and replayed turns beside the session's measured total, in one currency. Every figure is Simulated, not measured: it assumes the same conversation (A1: the other model gets the same prompts and answers with as many tokens, which it wouldn't) and the same token counts (A2); the answer lists every assumption. Say "would have cost about", never "would have cost". For the per-turn figures, the coverage reasons and the self-check, call replay_session with one model. A model no vendor profile lists refuses the whole comparison, with the reason.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.title: Estimate the cost of planned work
tools.description: Use to estimate what planned work on one project (id from list_projects) or repository (key from list_repositories) will cost: a p50–p90 range in USD at today's prices, never a single number, labelled "estimate". It is the median and 90th-percentile cost per active day (or per session) in the last 4 or 12 weeks × the planned active days (or sessions); days or sessions with any unpriced turn are left out and counted. With fewer than 5 known days or sessions there is no range: `refusal` says why. AI Credits are converted at 1 AI Credit = $0.01. With `model`, it estimates on that model instead: every session of the target in the window is replayed on it (as replay_session does) and the unit costs are the simulated ones, priced on each session's own channel as of when it ran (pricing "as-of-use"). Those figures are Simulated (same conversation and token counts assumed); `simulation` gives the method, the sessions and turns replayed, the rest by reason, how many self-checks passed, and the assumptions.

tools.name: explain_cost_change
tools.title: Explain why a cost changed
tools.description: Answers "costs went up 30%: was it a price change, more work, or a different model?" for one repository (key from list_repositories) or project (id from list_projects) between period A and period B. On the priced basis, as of use (tokens × the price version in force when each turn ran), per currency: the usage effect (more or fewer tokens at A's average price), the price effect (B's tokens × the change in unit price) and the mix effect (work moved between models), which add up exactly to the change; per model and token type (uncached input, cache read, cache write, output) with unit prices and the price versions behind them; turns without a priced figure counted as notExplained with reasons, never 0; and the documented price changes between the periods. Follow up with get_price_changes for the models with the largest price effect. Local repositories are named by folder only. Currencies stay apart unless currency is "usd" (1 AI Credit = $0.01).

tools.name: get_audit_rollup
tools.title: Get cross-session tool-call rollup
tools.description: Aggregates tool-call outcomes across one provider's most recent sessions in a date window: totals, failure rate, the top failing commands (and in how many sessions they failed), failures per day, a per-session summary, and breakdowns by tool, program and failure category. Sessions whose tool calls are unknown (a VS Code Agent Host session without a Copilot CLI event log) are not included in any count or rate; sessionsWithUnknownToolCalls says how many were left out and toolCallsUnavailableReason why. Use it for "which commands keep failing?".

tools.name: get_cost_rollup
tools.title: Get cross-session cost rollup
tools.description: Answers "what is driving my spend?" across every available provider (or one, with `provider`) in a date window, optionally for one repository or project: token and AI Credits totals with coverage, per-basis cost totals, cache hit ratio, spend by provider, model, day, repository, project, vendor and channel, the most expensive sessions, and `reconciliation` (Copilot's billed AI Credits against the price book, per model and month: a steady gap means the price book is out of date). Follow up with get_session_cost on a top session. The same data the web Dashboard shows. `active`: true marks a session whose latest turn started in the last 15 minutes; its figures may still change. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_price_book
tools.title: Get the price book
tools.description: Use to see which per-token prices the analyzer prices tokens with: each price version of a model on a channel ("github-copilot", "anthropic-api", ... or a user channel), its USD tiers per 1M tokens, the dates it is in force ([effectiveFrom, effectiveTo), UTC), its kind (list, promo, or the user's contract) and its cited sources with checkedAt. Default: every version on every channel. With `at`, only the versions in force then. A channel or model with no price is listed under `unknown` with the reason; it is unknown, never zero. Gaps between versions are listed under `gaps`, and user versions left out of the book under `problems`.

tools.name: get_price_changes
tools.title: Get price changes
tools.description: Use to see when a model's price changed. Two kinds, kept apart: documented (a boundary between two price-book versions: date, old and new USD per 1M tokens per token type, percentage, and the cited sources) and observed (GitHub Copilot only: billed AI Credits more than 5% above or below the price book for the same turns, the same way, 2 ISO weeks in a row with at least 20 such turns each; confidence "inferred", with the weeks as evidence: a prompt to check the price book, not a price). Oldest first. Observed changes read the sessions of every available provider (or one, with `provider`); documented ones read only the price book.

tools.name: get_project_cost
tools.title: Get a project's cost over time and breakdown
tools.description: Answers "what did this project cost, where did the money go?" for one project id from list_projects: everything get_repository_cost returns for the project's turns, plus a breakdown by repository member, by vendor then model, tokens per model by type (uncached input, cache write, cache read, reasoning, output) and the most expensive sessions. Defaults: monthly buckets, the preferred basis, prices as of use, native currencies. Returns totals per basis with coverage (knownTurns of turns), one point per bucket in the range (UTC; a bucket with turns but nothing known has usd null and no amounts: a gap, never 0) with a running total, a breakdown by vendor then model, and the documented price changes in the range for the models priced (priceChanges). Turns are bucketed by their own date; sessions are selected by their start. Local repositories are named by folder only. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_repository_cost
tools.title: Get a repository's cost over time
tools.description: Answers "what did this repository cost, and how did it change?" for one repository key from list_repositories, across every available provider unless `provider` is given. Defaults: monthly buckets, the preferred basis, prices as of use, native currencies. Returns totals per basis with coverage (knownTurns of turns), one point per bucket in the range (UTC; a bucket with turns but nothing known has usd null and no amounts: a gap, never 0) with a running total, a breakdown by vendor then model, and the documented price changes in the range for the models priced (priceChanges). Turns are bucketed by their own date; sessions are selected by their start. Local repositories are named by folder only. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_session_audit
tools.title: Get session tool-call audit
tools.description: Summarises how one session's tool calls went: totals by outcome (success/error/interrupted/denied/unknown), failure rate, breakdowns by tool, shell program and failure category (command-not-found, wrong-directory, invalid-arguments, dependency-missing, git-state, ...), per-turn counts, retried commands, the tokens spent recovering from failures, and outcome coverage. Start here for "why did the agent struggle?"; use list_tool_calls for the individual calls.

tools.name: get_session_cost
tools.title: Get session cost
tools.description: Explains what one session cost and why: token totals (uncached input, cache write, cache read, reasoning, output) and AI Credits, each with turn coverage; cache hit ratio; spend per model; the most expensive turns; cost-relevant events (compaction, cache expiry, model switch, ...); and context overhead (system-prompt parts, tools defined but never used); the session's repository and project. null means unknown, never zero — see unavailableReasons. `active`: true marks a session whose latest turn started in the last 15 minutes; its figures may still change. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_statement
tools.title: Get a project's billing statement
tools.description: Use to see what one project (id from list_projects) costs for a period: the frozen statement if the period is issued, with the re-run beside it and the exact diff (late logs, a price-book change), else the draft and whether it can be issued (only an ended period can). Lines per basis, currency, channel, model and price version with tokens and unit prices; turns with unknown cost listed with their reason, never counted as 0; subscription (API-equivalent) use left off unless the project includes it; the project's markup, fixed lines and own currency at its fixed rate; totals per currency; coverage; provenance (app version, price book, projects file, session ids). Months are calendar months in the statement's time zone. This tool never issues a statement: issuing is done in the app.

tools.name: get_turn
tools.title: Get one turn
tools.description: Reads one turn of a session: the user prompt and assistant response (secrets redacted, truncated to maxTextChars), its token usage and AI Credits, any triggered event (compaction, model switch, cache expiry, ...) and its tool calls with outcomes. The text and tool calls are unknown, with a reason, for a VS Code Agent Host turn whose Copilot CLI event log is missing, unreadable or has no match. Use it to explain why a turn found by get_session_cost or list_tool_calls was expensive or failed. `cost` gives the turn's billed, reported and priced figures (the priced one names its price version) and `preferredCost` the one totals use. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: list_findings
tools.title: List security, anomaly and behaviour-change findings
tools.description: Lists what the analyzer flagged across every available provider (or one) in a date window, most severe first: security (credential access, pipe-to-shell, destructive or history-rewriting commands, privilege escalation, data upload, ...), anomalies (cost or failure outliers), behaviour changes (first use of a program, tool or model) and price changes (kind "price-change": GitHub Copilot billing a model steadily above or below the price book, inferred; see get_price_changes). Each finding says what happened, when, in which session and turn, why it was flagged, with redacted evidence. Use get_turn to see the context.

tools.name: list_log_providers
tools.title: List log providers
tools.description: Lists the local agent-log sources (VS Code Copilot Chat, Claude Code CLI, pi, mitmproxy captures), whether each is available and why not, and which one is active. Use it to pick a `provider` argument or to explain why a source has no sessions.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: Lists the user's projects from their local projects file: each project's id, name and members (a repository key, optionally narrowed to a path inside it and branch patterns). A turn counts in at most one project, the most specific matching member. Use it to pick a `projectId` for list_repositories or list_sessions; `problems` lists what is wrong with the file, if anything. Client names and billing codes are not shared here; a statement (get_statement) has them.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: Lists the code repositories the sessions worked in, across every available provider unless `provider` is given: start here to find a `repository` key for list_sessions or to see which project each repository is in. Each entry has its key (a normalised remote such as github.com/org/app; a repository without a remote, or a folder outside one, is local:<folder name> or path:<folder name>), session and turn counts, first and last use, AI Credits with coverage (null is unknown, never zero) and project ids. Sessions with no repository are grouped by reason under `unattributed`. Local folder paths are never returned.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: Finds agent sessions of one provider, most recent first: start here to get the session ids every other per-session tool needs. Filter by a title/id substring, a start-date window, a repository and a project; each session names its repository key (null with unattributedReason when it has none) and project. `total` is the number of matches before `limit`, so you can tell whether to narrow the search.

tools.name: list_tool_calls
tools.title: List classified tool calls
tools.description: Lists one session's tool calls with outcome, exit code, failure category, a redacted stderr excerpt, the command and program, and the turn index. Filter by outcome, failure category, tool kind (shell, file-write, web, mcp, subagent, ...), tool name, shell program or turn; page with offset/limit (`total` counts every match). For a VS Code Agent Host session without a Copilot CLI event log the list is empty and toolCallsUnavailableReason says why: the calls are unknown, not zero.

tools.name: replay_session
tools.title: Replay a session on another model
tools.description: Use to see what one session (id from list_sessions) would have cost on another model: the session's own request trace (token counts only) is run through that model's vendor caching rules and priced, turn by turn beside what the session really cost. Every figure is Simulated, not measured: it assumes the same conversation (A1: the other model gets the same prompts and answers with as many tokens, which it wouldn't) and the same token counts (A2); the answer lists every assumption. Say "would have cost about", never "would have cost". The self-check (selfCheck) is the same replay on the session's own model compared with its log (cache read within 5%): if it didn't pass, trust the figures less; null when the own model has no vendor profile. Totals compare like with like (the turns replayed with a known measured and simulated cost); coverage gives the turns and requests not replayed with their reasons, and an unknown figure is null with a reason, never 0. A session whose provider's logs can't be replayed yet answers with the reason.

prompts.name: audit_session
prompts.title: Audit a session's tool calls
prompts.description: Explain why an agent session's tool calls failed and how to avoid it next time.

prompts.name: estimate_work
prompts.title: Estimate planned work
prompts.description: Give a cost range for planned work on a project, its inputs and the main uncertainty.

prompts.name: explain_cost_change
prompts.title: Explain why a cost changed
prompts.description: Say whether more work, a price change or a model change drove a repository's or project's cost between two periods, and what to do about each.

prompts.name: prepare_statement
prompts.title: Prepare a client statement
prompts.description: Summarise a project's statement for a period and draft a short note to the client.

prompts.name: review_costs
prompts.title: Review what drives my AI spend
prompts.description: Find the sessions, turns and habits that drive token and AI Credits spend, and suggest savings.

prompts.name: security_review
prompts.title: Review what my agents did that was risky
prompts.description: Review security findings: what happened, when, why it matters, and which guardrails would prevent it.

Default: every version on every channel. With `at`, only the versions in force then. A channel or model with no price is listed under `unknown` with the reason; it is unknown, never zero. Gaps between versions are listed under `gaps`, and user versions left out of the book under `problems`.

tools.name: get_price_changes
tools.title: Get price changes
tools.description: Use to see when a model's price changed. Two kinds, kept apart: documented (a boundary between two price-book versions: date, old and new USD per 1M tokens per token type, percentage, and the cited sources) and observed (GitHub Copilot only: billed AI Credits more than 5% above or below the price book for the same turns, the same way, 2 ISO weeks in a row with at least 20 such turns each; confidence "inferred", with the weeks as evidence: a prompt to check the price book, not a price). Oldest first. Observed changes read the sessions of every available provider (or one, with `provider`); documented ones read only the price book.

tools.name: get_project_cost
tools.title: Get a project's cost over time and breakdown
tools.description: Answers "what did this project cost, where did the money go?" for one project id from list_projects: everything get_repository_cost returns for the project's turns, plus a breakdown by repository member, by vendor then model, tokens per model by type (uncached input, cache write, cache read, reasoning, output) and the most expensive sessions. Defaults: monthly buckets, the preferred basis, prices as of use, native currencies. Returns totals per basis with coverage (knownTurns of turns), one point per bucket in the range (UTC; a bucket with turns but nothing known has usd null and no amounts: a gap, never 0) with a running total, a breakdown by vendor then model, and the documented price changes in the range for the models priced (priceChanges). Turns are bucketed by their own date; sessions are selected by their start. Local repositories are named by folder only. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_repository_cost
tools.title: Get a repository's cost over time
tools.description: Answers "what did this repository cost, and how did it change?" for one repository key from list_repositories, across every available provider unless `provider` is given. Defaults: monthly buckets, the preferred basis, prices as of use, native currencies. Returns totals per basis with coverage (knownTurns of turns), one point per bucket in the range (UTC; a bucket with turns but nothing known has usd null and no amounts: a gap, never 0) with a running total, a breakdown by vendor then model, and the documented price changes in the range for the models priced (priceChanges). Turns are bucketed by their own date; sessions are selected by their start. Local repositories are named by folder only. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_session_audit
tools.title: Get session tool-call audit
tools.description: Summarises how one session's tool calls went: totals by outcome (success/error/interrupted/denied/unknown), failure rate, breakdowns by tool, shell program and failure category (command-not-found, wrong-directory, invalid-arguments, dependency-missing, git-state, ...), per-turn counts, retried commands, the tokens spent recovering from failures, and outcome coverage. Start here for "why did the agent struggle?"; use list_tool_calls for the individual calls.

tools.name: get_session_cost
tools.title: Get session cost
tools.description: Explains what one session cost and why: token totals (uncached input, cache write, cache read, reasoning, output) and AI Credits, each with turn coverage; cache hit ratio; spend per model; the most expensive turns; cost-relevant events (compaction, cache expiry, model switch, ...); and context overhead (system-prompt parts, tools defined but never used); the session's repository and project. null means unknown, never zero — see unavailableReasons. `active`: true marks a session whose latest turn started in the last 15 minutes; its figures may still change. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_statement
tools.title: Get a project's billing statement
tools.description: Use to see what one project (id from list_projects) costs for a period: the frozen statement if the period is issued, with the re-run beside it and the exact diff (late logs, a price-book change), else the draft and whether it can be issued (only an ended period can). Lines per basis, currency, channel, model and price version with tokens and unit prices; turns with unknown cost listed with their reason, never counted as 0; subscription (API-equivalent) use left off unless the project includes it; the project's markup, fixed lines and own currency at its fixed rate; totals per currency; coverage; provenance (app version, price book, projects file, session ids). Months are calendar months in the statement's time zone. This tool never issues a statement: issuing is done in the app.

tools.name: get_turn
tools.title: Get one turn
tools.description: Reads one turn of a session: the user prompt and assistant response (secrets redacted, truncated to maxTextChars), its token usage and AI Credits, any triggered event (compaction, model switch, cache expiry, ...) and its tool calls with outcomes. The text and tool calls are unknown, with a reason, for a VS Code Agent Host turn whose Copilot CLI event log is missing, unreadable or has no match. Use it to explain why a turn found by get_session_cost or list_tool_calls was expensive or failed. `cost` gives the turn's billed, reported and priced figures (the priced one names its price version) and `preferredCost` the one totals use. Cost figures carry their basis: billed (what GitHub Copilot billed, AI Credits), reported (what the agent logged itself, USD) and priced (tokens × the price version in force on the turn's channel at the turn's time; see get_price_book, and priceVersionIds). The preferred figure is billed, else reported, else priced. A priced figure with apiEquivalent: true is what the same use costs on the API, though a flat-fee plan may have covered it. An unknown figure is {known:false, reason}, never 0; totals give knownTurns of turns per basis. Currencies stay apart; `usd` converts only at 1 AI Credit = $0.01.

tools.name: get_turn_series
tools.title: Get a session's per-turn series
tools.description: App-only: the per-turn figures (AI Credits, input, cache read, output, events) behind a session's cost chart. Called by the cost view, not by the model; use get_session_cost for the model-facing summary.

tools.name: list_findings
tools.title: List security, anomaly and behaviour-change findings
tools.description: Lists what the analyzer flagged across every available provider (or one) in a date window, most severe first: security (credential access, pipe-to-shell, destructive or history-rewriting commands, privilege escalation, data upload, ...), anomalies (cost or failure outliers), behaviour changes (first use of a program, tool or model) and price changes (kind "price-change": GitHub Copilot billing a model steadily above or below the price book, inferred; see get_price_changes). Each finding says what happened, when, in which session and turn, why it was flagged, with redacted evidence. Use get_turn to see the context.

tools.name: list_log_providers
tools.title: List log providers
tools.description: Lists the local agent-log sources (VS Code Copilot Chat, Claude Code CLI, pi, mitmproxy captures), whether each is available and why not, and which one is active. Use it to pick a `provider` argument or to explain why a source has no sessions.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: Lists the user's projects from their local projects file: each project's id, name and members (a repository key, optionally narrowed to a path inside it and branch patterns). A turn counts in at most one project, the most specific matching member. Use it to pick a `projectId` for list_repositories or list_sessions; `problems` lists what is wrong with the file, if anything. Client names and billing codes are not shared here; a statement (get_statement) has them.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: Lists the code repositories the sessions worked in, across every available provider unless `provider` is given: start here to find a `repository` key for list_sessions or to see which project each repository is in. Each entry has its key (a normalised remote such as github.com/org/app; a repository without a remote, or a folder outside one, is local:<folder name> or path:<folder name>), session and turn counts, first and last use, AI Credits with coverage (null is unknown, never zero) and project ids. Sessions with no repository are grouped by reason under `unattributed`. Local folder paths are never returned.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: Finds agent sessions of one provider, most recent first: start here to get the session ids every other per-session tool needs. Filter by a title/id substring, a start-date window, a repository and a project; each session names its repository key (null with unattributedReason when it has none) and project. `total` is the number of matches before `limit`, so you can tell whether to narrow the search.

tools.name: list_tool_calls
tools.title: List classified tool calls
tools.description: Lists one session's tool calls with outcome, exit code, failure category, a redacted stderr excerpt, the command and program, and the turn index. Filter by outcome, failure category, tool kind (shell, file-write, web, mcp, subagent, ...), tool name, shell program or turn; page with offset/limit (`total` counts every match). For a VS Code Agent Host session without a Copilot CLI event log the list is empty and toolCallsUnavailableReason says why: the calls are unknown, not zero.

tools.name: replay_session
tools.title: Replay a session on another model
tools.description: Use to see what one session (id from list_sessions) would have cost on another model: the session's own request trace (token counts only) is run through that model's vendor caching rules and priced, turn by turn beside what the session really cost. Every figure is Simulated, not measured: it assumes the same conversation (A1: the other model gets the same prompts and answers with as many tokens, which it wouldn't) and the same token counts (A2); the answer lists every assumption. Say "would have cost about", never "would have cost". The self-check (selfCheck) is the same replay on the session's own model compared with its log (cache read within 5%): if it didn't pass, trust the figures less; null when the own model has no vendor profile. Totals compare like with like (the turns replayed with a known measured and simulated cost); coverage gives the turns and requests not replayed with their reasons, and an unknown figure is null with a reason, never 0. A session whose provider's logs can't be replayed yet answers with the reason.
